items.t: CoreWeave, Broadcom, Verizon among nine companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE
items.x: Applied Optoelectronics told the WSJ it objected because it was unsure how tokenization would affect its stock price, liquidity and volatility.

items.t: Trump waives broad new Russia sanctions, Zelenskyy condemns it as 'wrong'
items.x: Trump signed the Graham Bill, which targeted Russia over its invasion of Ukraine, into law in September.

items.t: Turkey confirms Hex founder Richard Heart’s arrest, says police seized $7.15 million and six cold wallets
items.x: Police reportedly seized $7.15 million in cash, six cold wallets, seven firearms and 1,400 rounds of ammunition in searches of 15 addresses.

items.t: Crypto Super PAC Fairshake Pours Millions More Into Defeating Sherrod Brown
items.x: An FEC filing shows the Fairshake affiliate Defend American Jobs disclosed roughly $7 million more in ads against the Ohio Democrat, pushing its total past $46 million—days after the PAC expanded its map to 32 House races.

items.t: Goldman, Wells Fargo, Morgan Stanley see tokenization as a growth play, not a threat
items.x: The largest banks in the world are eyeing new trading opportunities, speeding up payments and a role for advisers as tokenization takes root in Wall Street.

items.t: Semiconductor market to remain solid ‘at least through next year,’ South Korea finance minister says
items.x: South Korea's finance minister said semiconductor growth can last at least through 2027 as supply remains tight despite a global chip sell-off.

items.t: Crypto Firms Launch Quantum Alliance as 6 Million Bitcoin Sit Exposed
items.x: The nine-member group, modeled on the Internet Engineering Task Force, aims to set open standards for testing quantum-resistance claims as forecasts place the first practical attack in the late 2020s.

items.t: AI stocks plunge. Inflation heats up. Where we're still finding opportunities
items.x: The sinking AI trade rattled last week's market. But solid bank earnings and a rotation beyond tech gave us reasons for optimism.

items.t: Chinese Startup StepFun Launches a Phone Built Around an AI Agent, Not Apps
items.x: StepFun's STEPX Neo opened for pre-orders in China on Oct. 13 at 3,999 yuan, with an AI agent built into the operating system instead of bolted on as an app.

items.t: 'Dead money’ for a decade: Why this hedge fund approach may deliver an advantage over bonds
items.x: Investors may want to rethink their bond allocation and opt for managed futures exposure.

items.t: Citrini sees a tokenization boom. The harder question is who profits
items.x: The influential research firm says real-world assets could finally give blockchains a clear role in finance. For investors, the next challenge is figuring out which companies, networks and protocols capture the revenue.

items.t: Polygon sees Coinme acquisition as entry to payments sector dominated by Visa, Stripe
items.x: CEO Marc Boiron said the Coinme acquisition will help Polygon control customer relationships and capture revenue that previously went to payment intermediaries.
